Theorem
[Higher global regularity] 1. ch8:8.13\group ch08-generalized-solutions Under the hypotheses of Theorem 8.10, also assume $\partial \Omega \in C^{k+2}$ and $u-\varphi \in W_0^{1,2}(\Omega )$ for some $\varphi \in W^{k+2,2}(\Omega )$. Then $u\in W^{k+2,2}(\Omega )$ and \begin{equation} \| u\| _{W^{k+2,2}(\Omega )}\leq C\bigl(\| u\| _{L^2(\Omega )} +\| f\| _{W^{k,2}(\Omega )}+\| \varphi \| _{W^{k+2,2}(\Omega )}\bigr). \tag {8.27} \end{equation} Here $C=C(n,\lambda ,K,k,\partial \Omega )$. If the coefficients, $f$, $\varphi $, and $\partial \Omega $ are smooth, then $u\in C^\infty (\overline\Omega )$.
Proof

\sketch Iterate the tangential differentiation and normal recovery argument from Theorem 8.12, then apply Sobolev embedding in the smooth case.

□
